For example, `organizations/123456789012/customConstraints/custom.createOnlyE2TypeVms`. Must contain 1 to 62 characters, excluding the prefix `organizations/{organization_id}/customConstraints/custom.`.

methodTypes.description: The types of operations that the constraint applies to.

enumDescriptions: Default value. This value is unused.
Constraint applied when creating the resource.
Constraint applied when updating the resource.
Not supported. Constraint applied when deleting the resource.

resourceTypes.description: Immutable. The resource type that the constraint applies to, in the format `{canonical_service_name}/{resource_type_name}`. For example, `compute.googleapis.com/Instance`.

condition.description: A Common Expression Language (CEL) condition expression that must evaluate to `true` for the constraint to be enforced. The maximum length is 1000 characters. For example: + `resource.instanceName.matches('(production|test)_(.+_)?[\d]+')`: Evaluates to `true` if the resource's `instanceName` attribute contains the following: + The prefix `production` or `test` + An underscore (`_`) + Optional: One or more characters, followed by an underscore (`_`) + One or more digits + `resource.management.auto_upgrade == true`: Evaluates to `true` if the resource's `management.auto_upgrade` attribute is `true`.

GoogleCloudSecuritypostureV1CustomConstr.description: A custom, user-defined constraint. You can apply the constraint only to the resource types specified in the constraint, and only within the organization where the constraint is defined. _When you create a custom constraint, it is not enforced automatically._ You must use an organization policy to [enforce the constraint](https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/help/organization-policy/constraints/enforce).

constraint.description: Information about the constraint that was violated. The format of this information can change at any time without prior notice. Your application must not depend on this information in any way.

PostureDeployment.description: Details for a Posture deployment on an organization, folder, or project. You can deploy at most one posture to each organization, folder, or project. The parent resource for a posture deployment is always the organization, even if the deployment applies to a folder or project.

desiredPostureId.description: Output only. The posture ID that was specified for the deployment. Present only if the posture deployment is in a failed state.

etag.description: Optional. An opaque identifier for the current version of the posture deployment. To prevent concurrent updates from overwriting each other, always provide the `etag` when you update a posture deployment. You can also provide the `etag` when you delete a posture deployment, to help ensure that you're deleting the intended posture deployment.

postureRevisionId.description: Required. The revision ID of the posture used in the deployment.

reconciling.description: Output only. Whether the posture deployment is in the process of being updated.

targetResource.description: Required. The organization, folder, or project where the posture is deployed. Uses one of the following formats: * `organizations/{organization_number}` * `folders/{folder_number}` * `projects/{project_number}`

postureId.description: Required. The posture used in the deployment, in the format `organizations/{organization}/locations/global/postures/{posture_id}`.
